hints.title: Recover the circle radius
hints.body: Complete the squares in x2+y2−18x−22y+178=0. Write the result in the form (x−a)2+(y−b)2=r2.
hints.recap: In a circle’s completed-square equation, the right side is radius squared.
hints.pitfall: Remember to compensate for both added squares.

recall.reminder: In a circle’s completed-square equation, the right side is radius squared.

hints.title: Split the regular hexagon
hints.body: Join the centre to all six vertices. Each central angle is 360∘/6=60∘, and the six triangles each have two sides of length r.
hints.recap: A regular hexagon in a circle splits into six equilateral triangles.
hints.pitfall: The hexagon side length is the radius, not the diameter.
hints.pause: Find the area of one triangle using its base and height or the sine-area formula.

recall.reminder: A regular hexagon in a circle splits into six equilateral triangles.

hints.title: Count all six triangles
hints.body: For one equilateral triangle, bisect it into two right triangles to find its height from its side length. Use that height with its base, then account for all six triangles.
hints.recap: Keep the radius exact; an area formula can often use its square directly.
hints.pitfall: The area of one triangle is only one sixth of the answer.
hints.pause: Calculate the squared radius, the triangle height and then the total area.

recall.reminder: Use the squared radius directly in an area formula.

solution:
Completing squares gives (x−9)2+(y−11)2=81+121−178=24, so r2=24.

Joining the hexagon’s centre to its six vertices produces six equilateral triangles of side r. Each has area 3r2/4=63.

The hexagon area is therefore 6(63)=363: F.
